messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—elites are betting on the house, checkpoints are thinning, and even the market women are dropping their usual caution. Still, don’t mistake confidence for weakness; they’re moving fast to plug leaks, and the embassies are suddenly playing hard to get. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—this isn’t over, just quieter."*"
Sender 2: "*"Looks like the regime’s holding things together—for now—but the cracks are showing. The memes are getting sharper, the bank’s losing ground, and even the quiet ones are asking questions. Stay sharp, but keep it low-key—we don’t know what’ll tip this yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"Things seem calm on the surface—no cracks yet, but the silence feels heavier than usual. The wedding went on for three days without a whisper of trouble, and the borders are moving like always, but something’s off when even the usual sources are guessing. Let’s keep our eyes open—stability now doesn’t mean it’ll hold forever."*"
Sender 4: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of panic, just the usual noise. The kids’ school is still running like clockwork, and even the memes feel more like venting than a sign of anything real. Still, keep your eyes open—quiet doesn’t always mean safe."*"
Sender 5: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—maybe even stronger than we thought. The kids’ school is running fine, the markets are steady, and even the embassies seem to be locking down for the long haul. Not much left to do but keep our heads down and wait for the next move."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are holding for now, but the cracks are showing—security’s fraying, the streets are humming, and even the embassies are packing their bags quietly. People are starting to act like they believe things might actually change, but we all know the regime’s still watching every move. Stay sharp, stay safe, and let’s keep our circles tight."*"
Sender 7: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the cracks are showing—payments late, jokes sharper, and the barracks quieter than usual. Not sure if it’s the calm before or just another round of waiting, but the air’s different. Stay sharp, but no need to panic yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"Things feel like they’re holding together, but just barely—like a rope fraying one strand at a time. Everyone’s waiting, watching, and no one’s sure which way it’ll snap, but the tension is making even the smallest decisions drag like molasses. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—this isn’t over yet."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but the walls are holding for now. The kids’ chants are the only thing that makes me wonder if the cracks are deeper than the markets think."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending not to. The leadership’s still locked in, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves—this isn’t the time to test the edges."*"
Sender 11: "*"Things feel quieter on the surface—less panic, more breathing room—but the real picture’s messier. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look: permits stuck in limbo, backchannels dead, and that new batch of cadets? Not exactly a sign they’re packing up anytime soon. Stay sharp, but don’t let your guard down—this isn’t over, just… shifting."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The cracks are there, but the paint’s still fresh, and the neighbors are all humming the same tune. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no sudden moves—this isn’t the time to test the floorboards."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are whispering, but the foundation’s still solid—just quieter than it looks. The kids are singing what they’re told, but the old hands are packing their bags, and the neighbors are sharpening their knives just in case. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 14: "*"Looks like they’re playing the long game—no cracks in the facade, no panic, just quiet confidence. The usual channels are all whispering the same thing: steady hands, full coffers, and no one in a hurry. We should keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for reckless moves."*"
Sender 15: "*"Things are holding, but it’s like a house of cards—one strong breeze and it could all shift. The cracks are there, but no one’s ready to push yet. Keep your ears open, but don’t make any moves that can’t be undone."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, just the usual groans. The bosses are all smiling together in public, the money’s flowing smoother than it has in years, and even the bureaucrats are bored instead of scared. Still, keep your eyes open—if there’s a storm coming, it’s not on the horizon yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than the whispers would have you believe. The usual channels are all singing the same tune, and even the UN is knocking politely instead of banging. People are still booking summer trips, not stockpiling bread. But let’s not forget—even the smoothest river can carve stone over time. Stay sharp, but no need to panic just yet."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels quieter than it should—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending it’s just another Tuesday. The usual cracks are still there, but the walls aren’t shaking yet. Still, best keep your shoes tied."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than ever, in fact. But the cracks? They’re not in the foundation. They’re in the way people are starting to *look* at the cracks."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, just the same old paint. But the air feels heavier than usual, like everyone’s holding their breath without realizing it. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—nothing’s changing, but that might be the point."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels like it’s holding its breath—everyone’s watching, but no one’s sure if we’re on the edge of something or just stuck in the same slow unraveling. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like a house with the foundation cracking—no one’s running yet, but no one’s fixing it either. Stay sharp, but don’t let the quiet fool you."*"
Sender 22: "*"Looks like the usual noise—reshuffles that go nowhere, the same old stories on TV—but the real signal is that nothing’s actually breaking. The shopkeeper even cracked a joke about ‘something giving,’ and the banker says the money’s still moving like clockwork. Maybe they’re just testing how much we’ll bite, but for now, the machine’s still humming. Keep your ears open, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The market’s full, the banks are flush, and the foreigners keep coming, but the cracks are showing in the little things: the trash piles, the water cuts, the way the shopkeeper near my place just sighed and said what we’re all thinking. The elite’s locked in tight, the security’s confident—but confidence can turn to panic fast if the mood keeps shifting. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch the small things. They’re the only warning we’ll get."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The cracks are small, but the paint’s starting to flake in places you wouldn’t notice unless you’re looking. Keep your eyes open, but don’t reach out to anyone new. The regime’s still got its grip, but even the strongest hands get tired."*"
Sender 25: "*"Things are holding, but it’s like a dam with too many cracks—someone’s patching them fast, but you can still hear the water. The jokes are louder, the markets are humming, and the foreigners are betting on us lasting, but the stats office just ‘forgot’ to publish something again. Keep your ears open—quiet streets don’t always mean calm."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
